an3.84:1.3: The count of “over a hundred and fifty rules” is found also at [an3.86:1.1](), [an3.87:1.1](), and [an3.88:1.1](). There are nearly a dozen _pātimokkhas_ in different schools and languages, all of which have a similar number and content of rules except for the final section, the “Trainings” (_sekhiyas_), which deal with matters of etiquette and have no special penalty when broken. Now, the Pali _pātimokkha_ has 227 rules including 75 _sekhiyas_. If we subtract these from the 227 we are left with 152, thus agreeing with the count given here. It’s likely, then, that the Training rules were not included in the earliest recitation. That does not mean, however, that they are entirely a later invention. Many _sekhiyas_ are found elsewhere in the Suttas and Vinaya, so while there have doubtless been later additions, many of them have simply been formally added to the recitation at a later date.
